title: Toric-code stabilizers and the exact limits of local protection
status: Developed classical result with a checked example; historical claims corrected where needed
summary: The historical claim of going beyond toric code needs a baseline with a defined lattice, code space, and error model. The square torus code has exact commuting stabilizers and nonlocal logical operators; these properties can be proved at the Pauli-algebra level.
definitions: Place one qubit on every edge of an L×L square lattice with periodic boundaries,L≥3.
For a vertexv setA_v=∏_{e incident v}X_e; for a plaquettep setB_p=∏_{e∈∂p}Z_e.

result.name: Commuting stabilizers and distanceL
result.statement: AllA_v andB_p commute. Their common+1eigenspace encodes two qubits, and a shortest noncontractible Pauli loop has lengthL, giving code distanceL.
result.proof: X andZ anticommute on one edge. A star and plaquette share either zero or two edges, so their commutation sign is(+1)or(−1)²=+1. Products of all stars and all plaquettes each equalI because every edge occurs twice. On the connected torus these are the only independent relations of each type; thus the stabilizer rank is2L²−2 among2L²qubits and the code dimension is2². AZ string anticommutes with stars at its endpoints, detecting open-string errors; a closed string commutes with all stars. Contractible loops are products of plaquettes and act trivially on the code. A noncontractible loop cannot be such a boundary and acts logically. The shortest noncontractible direct or dual cycle hasLedges, yielding the minimum nontrivial logical Pauli weightL.

example.setup: TakeL=3 and follow a Z string along one periodic row.
example.calculation: There are18edge qubits,9stars,and9plaquettes,with16independent stabilizers and a four-dimensional code space. A one-edgeZerror creates two violated star syndromes; a length-three wrappedZloop has no syndrome but changes a logical state. Thus local detectability and logical vulnerability coexist exactly as the distance statement predicts.
example.conclusion: The baseline protection is a precise code-space statement against bounded-weight Pauli errors, not an unrestricted immunity claim.

limits: This does not prove passive self-correction at nonzero temperature, nor protection against arbitrary correlated errors. The MPPF proposal had no recovered code, stabilizers, or distance certificate with which to establish an improvement.
extension: For a claimed extension, provide its commuting constraints or alternative code definition, count independent logical degrees of freedom, and exhibit both a lower bound and a matching logical operator for its distance.

title: Running-coupling factors and the logarithm convention
status: Developed classical result with a checked example; historical claims corrected where needed
summary: The recovered formula wrote a coupling with log(μ²/Λ²) while also giving a derivative with respect to logμ. These logarithm conventions differ by a factor of two. Direct integration identifies the consistent prefactor and avoids importing a numerical physics claim.
definitions: Assume dα/dlogμ=−(β₀/(2π))α², withβ₀constant.
The reference scaleΛ is defined by the integration constant; the formula is used only where its denominator is nonzero.

result.proof: Differentiate1/α with respect tologμ to getβ₀/(2π). Integration gives1/α=(β₀/(2π))log(μ/Λ), proving the first expression. Since log(μ²/Λ²)=2log(μ/Λ), the second expression follows. example.conclusion: The exact integration resolves the historical normalization ambiguity and provides a reusable consistency check.

limits: The equation is an assumed truncated model. It does not establish a continuum quantum field theory or validate a measured strong coupling at any scale. The number of flavors and matching thresholds would require further physical input.

title: A finite Stinespring dilation with a complete channel calculation
status: Developed classical result with a checked example; historical claims corrected where needed
summary: The recovered operator-theoretic request included Stinespring alongside transfer and quiver coefficients. A finite channel has a complete elementary dilation proof. Arbitrary transfer matrices do not automatically preserve density matrices; positivity and normalization must be checked.
definitions: A Kraus map isΦ(ρ)=Σ_aK_aρK_a*, withΣ_aK_a*K_a=I.
A density matrix is positive semidefinite with trace one; an auxiliary environment has orthonormal basis|a⟩.

result.name: Exact isometric dilation
result.statement: DefineVψ=Σ_aK_aψ⊗|a⟩. ThenV*V=I andΦ(ρ)=Tr_env(VρV*). In particular the map is trace-preserving and completely positive.
result.proof: For vectorsψ,φ, orthogonality of|a⟩ gives⟨Vψ,Vφ⟩=Σ_a⟨ψ,K_a*K_aφ⟩=⟨ψ,φ⟩, proving the isometry. ExpandingVρV* produces termsK_aρK_b*⊗|a⟩⟨b|; partial tracing keeps exactlya=b, yieldingΦ. Positivity holds after adjoining any finite ancilla because the extended map is a sum of terms(I⊗K_a)R(I⊗K_a)* forR≥0. Trace preservation follows from cyclicity and the normalizationΣK_a*K_a=I. This constructs the finite dilation directly rather than invoking an unspecified continuum theorem.

example.setup: TakeK₀=√p I andK₁=√(1−p)Z, with0≤p≤1, acting on a qubit.

example.conclusion: The state map has an exact dilation and normalization proof, giving a rigorous template for any recovered operator proposal.
